# Applied R

Applied R is part of the UoN Digital Skills programme. It provides a practical route into R programming for research and data analysis. Start with the [Course Overview](index.qmd) for the lesson sequence and intended audience.

## What This Course Contains

This course section of the site contains:

- four session pages for the Applied R pathway: foundations, functions, iteration and data analysis
- a compatibility page retaining the former standalone variables URL
- learner setup, reference, discussion and additional practice material
- instructor notes and optional teaching extensions
- course-level information about contribution, conduct, licensing, and learner profiles

## Course Scope

The course supports participants to:

- build confidence with core R programming concepts
- work more effectively with objects, functions, loops, and tidyverse workflows
- develop more reproducible analytical habits
- connect programming practice to real research workflows

## Adaptation and Attribution

This local course is substantially adapted from Software Carpentry's `r-novice-inflammation` lesson.

The UoN version reorganises, extends, and contextualises that material into four sessions for local delivery in the Methods for Data Science pathway. Each session has a 100-minute plan: 60 minutes teaching, 30 minutes activities including debriefs, and a separate 10-minute break. The foundations and Gapminder examples also draw on Software Carpentry's `r-novice-gapminder` materials.

- Upstream lesson repository: <https://github.com/swcarpentry/r-novice-inflammation>
- Upstream lesson site: <https://swcarpentry.github.io/r-novice-inflammation/>
- Gapminder lesson site: <https://swcarpentry.github.io/r-novice-gapminder/>
